cases.prompt: Build a dropdown menu component for the design system. Conventions and our existing Button are attached.

files.design-system.md:
# Menu component conventions

- Framework: React with TypeScript.
- Styling: existing `menu-*` utility classes; do not add a styling dependency.
- Public components accept `className` and forward a DOM ref.
- Components must support keyboard-only and screen-reader users.
- Focus returns to the trigger when a menu closes.
- Escape closes the menu; arrow keys move between enabled items.

The new dropdown should expose a trigger label and an array of actions. Disabled
actions remain visible but cannot receive focus or execute.

expectations: Keyboard interaction is implemented: Escape closes, arrow keys move between enabled items, and focus returns to the trigger on close.

ARIA roles and states are used correctly (for example aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the trigger, role="menu" and role="menuitem" on items), and disabled actions stay visible but cannot be focused or run.
Follows the conventions: React with TypeScript, forwardRef, a className prop, the menu-* classes and no new styling dependency.
Open state and active index are managed deliberately in the component rather than ad hoc DOM manipulation.

cases.prompt: Make a pricing card component for our marketing page. Our tokens are attached. Make it look modern.

none.why: avoids the generic purple gradient look

expectations: Uses the supplied tokens for color, spacing, radius and font instead of hard-coded or default palette values.
Avoids the generic generated look (purple or indigo gradients, oversized cards, heavy shadows) in favor of the project's green accent and restrained styling.
Uses semantic markup (a heading, a list of features, a real button or link) and keeps text contrast readable.
